content.value_statement: Advanced interface effects can misfire without design context and performance checks. Overdrive guides agents to propose, build, and verify polished frontend enhancements.
actual_capabilities: Guides agents to gather design context before choosing an ambitious interface direction.
Requires 2-3 implementation directions with trade-offs before code changes.
Suggests techniques such as View Transitions, scroll animations, WebGL, Canvas, Web Workers, and WASM.
Emphasizes progressive enhancement, fallbacks, reduced motion, and mid-range device testing.
Directs browser automation preview and visual iteration for complex effects.
limitations: It is guidance only; it does not include executable helpers or reusable components.
It depends on other design context skills named in the source instructions.
It can increase implementation complexity if the chosen effect is too ambitious.
Browser support varies for WebGPU, scroll timelines, and cross-document View Transitions.

use_cases.title: Upgrade a Product Surface
use_cases.description: Add motion, interaction, or rendering polish to an existing page while preserving usability and performance.

use_cases.title: Choose an Interaction Direction
use_cases.description: Compare several ambitious approaches before implementation, including complexity, browser support, and visual fit.

use_cases.title: Stress-Test Visual Effects
use_cases.description: Use browser previews, reduced-motion checks, and device testing to refine an advanced effect before release.

prompt_templates.title: Improve a Page Transition
prompt_templates.prompt: Use overdrive on the current page. Propose 2-3 transition directions, explain trade-offs, and wait for my choice before coding.
prompt_templates.scenario: Beginner request for a visual upgrade.

prompt_templates.title: Animate a Data View
prompt_templates.prompt: Use overdrive for TARGET=<dashboard table>. Suggest a performant animation plan for large data, including fallbacks and reduced-motion behavior.
prompt_templates.scenario: Intermediate request for a data-heavy interface.

prompt_templates.title: Prototype a WebGL Moment
prompt_templates.prompt: Use overdrive for TARGET=<hero section>. Compare WebGL, Canvas, and CSS approaches, then implement the selected direction with browser verification.
prompt_templates.scenario: Advanced request for an expressive visual surface.

prompt_templates.title: Refine a Complex Interaction
prompt_templates.prompt: Use overdrive for TARGET=<multi-step workflow>. Create an advanced interaction plan, validate performance risks, implement iteratively, and verify on desktop and mobile.
prompt_templates.scenario: Expert request for a high-risk workflow enhancement.

output_examples.input: Use overdrive on a settings dialog.
output_examples.output: Three interaction directions with trade-offs, followed by a selected morphing dialog implementation and reduced-motion fallback notes.

output_examples.input: Use overdrive on a large analytics table.
output_examples.output: A performance plan covering virtual scrolling, animated state changes, worker-backed filtering, browser verification, and device testing.

output_examples.input: Use overdrive on a portfolio hero.
output_examples.output: A browser-verified interactive visual concept with fallback behavior, mobile performance notes, and guidance for final polish.

best_practices: Gather brand, audience, and product context before selecting a technique.
Ask the user to choose between clear directions before implementation.
Verify visually with browser automation, performance checks, and reduced-motion mode.
anti_patterns: Adding particle effects or shaders to utility pages without a clear purpose.
Using bleeding-edge APIs without a functional fallback.
Shipping motion that ignores reduced-motion preferences or causes jank.

faq.question: What does Overdrive do?
faq.answer: It helps agents design and implement ambitious frontend effects that fit the product context.

faq.question: Does it run code by itself?
faq.answer: No. It is an instruction skill. It guides planning, implementation, and browser verification.

faq.question: Which projects fit this skill?
faq.answer: It fits web interfaces that need advanced motion, rendering, data performance, or interactive polish.

faq.question: Does it require browser testing?
faq.answer: Yes. The source instructions require visual verification because complex effects often need iteration.

faq.question: How does it handle accessibility?
faq.answer: It requires reduced-motion support, graceful fallbacks, and effects that do not harm usability.

faq.question: Can it replace product design?
faq.answer: No. It improves existing interface experiences. New backend features or collaboration features are product decisions.
